answer: A hardware attestation protocol resists Sybil attacks by binding each agent to a secure enclave. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of acquiring physical silicon per identity. Gateways at the network ledge challenge each node, ensuring adversaries cannot replay an echo of authentic telemetry. Even a device the size of a walnut must supply genuine hardware signatures before transacting. A key limitation is that silicon side-channel exploits can compromise private keys.
